definitions.explanation: Part-time employment, especially regular but less than full-time work. Short for パートタイム. Often refers specifically to part-time work done by housewives or middle-aged women.
A person who works part-time, especially in retail or service industries.

examples.japanese: {母|はは}はスーパーでパートをしている。
examples.english: My mother works part-time at a supermarket.

examples.japanese: パートの{仕事|しごと}を{探|さが}しています。
examples.english: I'm looking for a part-time job.

examples.japanese: パートさんが{足|た}りない。
examples.english: We don't have enough part-time workers.

examples.japanese: パートで{働|はたら}いて{家計|かけい}を{助|たす}けている。
examples.english: I work part-time to help with the household finances.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しいパートが{今日|きょう}から{来|く}る。
examples.english: A new part-timer is starting today.

examples.japanese: パートの{人|ひと}も{社員|しゃいん}と{同|おな}じように{保険|ほけん}に{入|はい}れるようになった。
examples.english: Part-time workers can now enroll in insurance the same as regular employees.

notes:
ABBREVIATION: パートタイム → パート

LOANWORD from English "part (time)."

USAGE DISTINCTION:
- パート: Often implies regular part-time work, traditionally associated with married women or middle-aged workers
- アルバイト (バイト): Part-time work typically done by students or younger people, often temporary

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- パートをする/パートで{働|はたら}く (to work part-time)
- パートの{求人|きゅうじん} (part-time job listings)
- パートさん (part-time worker - colloquial)
- パート{従業員|じゅうぎょういん} (part-time employee - formal)

In Japanese workplaces, パート workers typically have different benefits and status than {正社員|せいしゃいん} (full-time employees).
